destination.question: How do holonomy, boundary conditions and quantum effects determine surviving supersymmetry, radius dynamics and instability diagnostics?
destination.summary: Spinor counting, radiative stabilization, instanton-generated decompactification and winding instabilities are distinct fine questions. Proposed links between physical stability and supersymmetry remain conjectural.

conventions: Supersymmetry of a parent theory, a vacuum and a limiting configuration must be distinguished.
excludes: An established prediction of low-energy supersymmetry
A universal equivalence between special holonomy and complete physical stability

Nonzero spinorial invariants force parallel spinors if a Ricci-flat metric exists.

evidence.text: Construct invariant forms through Maurer–Cartan equations and shifted orbifold actions, solve the geometric supersymmetry conditions in terms of fluxes, and obtain scalar spectra from the normalized Hessian of the real-superpotential potential. Appendix A reduces a solvmanifold Laplacian equation to a Mathieu equation.

sources.title: Instabilities in scale-separated Casimir vacua

evidence.text: Einstein-frame dimensional reduction and canonical kinetic normalization precede the Hessian mass calculation. The dangerous shape-mode curvature is obtained by numerical quadrature and a centered finite difference with step 10^-5.

sources.title: Scale-separated AdS$_2$ flux vacua from type II

evidence.text: Dimensional reduction of the democratic type II pseudo-action in ten-dimensional Einstein frame, imposing RR duality after variation. The resulting two-dimensional dilaton-gravity action retains the volume-dependent Ricci coupling; a real superpotential is constructed to reproduce flux, curvature, and source contributions.

sources.title: Supersymmetric scale-separated AdS$_{3}$ orientifold vacua of type IIB

evidence.text: Use bispinor/Killing-spinor supersymmetry conditions together with the sourced Bianchi identity. In the smeared approximation gs F3=(W1/6)Φ−⋆W27; μ²=LAdS^−2 and W1=(12/7)μe^−A.

sources.title: Instabilities in scale-separated Casimir vacua

evidence.text: One-loop trace-log and Schwinger proper-time representations are related to heat kernels and propagators. Image sums, Jacobi theta functions, Epstein zeta functions and Poisson resummation organize the torus Casimir energy; individual contributions are regulated by subtracting the corresponding uncompactified geometry.

sources.title: Instabilities in scale-separated Casimir vacua

evidence.text: For traceless internal perturbations, the kinetic-operator correction is L1 = -∂i(hij∂j). Linearized kernel and propagator equations handle degenerate spectra without diagonalizing the perturbation. Fourier-mode estimates bound the response and support the claimed existence of its first functional derivative.
